title: Authenticode root-cause closure, signing evidence-contract integrity, and operational acceptance readiness

baseline.worktree_state_at_start: restored from a sandbox re-clone; reconciled non-destructively to the remote tip (tar snapshot taken first, then git reset --mixed FETCH_HEAD); 924 tracked files, clean status
baseline.ci_evidence_rule: the exact-SHA Source and Windows runs for this mission are recorded only in the mission report and in the generated acceptance-report.json, never in this file

recovery_rule: no reset --hard, no git clean, no force-push, no amend or rebase of published commits; every change is an ordinary commit on the release branch

retrieval_attempts: curl -sIL on the artifact archive_download_url: HTTP 303 to productionresultssa5.blob.core.windows.net, then curl --http1.1 --tlsv1.2 on the signed blob URL returned 'curl (35) SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL' with http=000 and 0 bytes
gh run download <Windows run> from inside the repository: 'unexpected EOF'
gh api <repository>/actions/jobs/<job>/logs: the same blob host returned EOF
readable_channels: check-run metadata and annotations via api.github.com (artifact metadata and the four annotation titles were read successfully)
authenticode_attribution.mechanism_established_in_source: SIGNATURE_QUERY_SCRIPT asked Get-AuthenticodeSignature without -ErrorAction Stop and without try/catch, so any statement-level failure left $signature null, the hashtable still serialised, and powershell.exe exited 0 with {"Status":"","StatusMessage":"","SignerSubject":null}; run_powershell discarded stderr whenever stdout parsed, so the harness recorded status UNKNOWN with an empty status_message and the step stayed green. The shape is proven from the shipped code; whether it is what happened on the runner cannot be confirmed without that run's stderr.
ruled_out: an encoding or JSON-parse failure of the harness: the tool-version query in the same run used the identical run_powershell path and returned a parseable payload
a mutation of published artifacts: none was attempted or performed
authenticode_attribution.resolution_path: the next exact-SHA Windows run is self-attributing: the query reports QueryError, the harness carries bounded redacted stderr and the exit code, and the capability probe publishes the PowerShell version and cmdlet availability into signing-status.json, the job console line, the step summary and the Signature status annotation

defects.symptom: an exit-0 query with an empty Status produced status UNKNOWN with an empty reason, and the step was green
defects.root_cause: run_powershell returned the parsed payload as soon as stdout was valid JSON, discarding stderr whenever the exit code was 0; the query script never reported its own statement-level failure
defects.fix: the query script runs Get-AuthenticodeSignature -ErrorAction Stop inside try/catch and publishes QueryError; run_powershell attaches bounded, redacted powershell_stderr plus powershell_exit_code to any payload produced with a non-empty error channel and accepts a required_field whose absence is itself an error; run_signing prefers the script's own error record, then stderr, then the harness message

defects.symptom: a legitimate raw Unknown (or any spelling the aggregator did not know) folded into aggregate FAIL, reporting an unattributable answer as a confirmed signature failure
defects.root_cause: the per-file 'status' field held the raw Windows string and aggregate_signing_status compared raw sets such as {'NotSigned'} and {'Valid'}
defects.fix: one shared, case-insensitive normalizer in packaging/release_metadata.py maps Valid/Ok to PASS, NotSigned to UNSIGNED, a mismatch or untrusted chain to FAIL, and Unknown, UnknownError or any unrecognised spelling to UNKNOWN; raw_status keeps the Windows answer verbatim with raw_status_recognized

defects.symptom: read_signing_evidence accepted an aggregate the per-file rows contradicted and carried a second aggregation implementation for records without one
defects.root_cause: the report re-derived a verdict with its own raw-spelling rule, so two owners of one vocabulary could disagree
defects.fix: the report validates the document with the shared validator and refuses any contradiction; the fallback rule is deleted, so a record is either contract-valid or an evidence error

defects.symptom: the report normalizer kept only filename, status and signer, so the published acceptance report could not explain any state
defects.root_cause: fields were whitelisted away during normalization
defects.fix: SIGNING_FILE_EVIDENCE_FIELDS retains status_message, raw_status, raw_status_recognized, provenance, both digests and the container binding, plus the document-level harness, policy, counts and binding fields

defects.symptom: no schema identity or version check existed for the signing document, and a required reason was not enforceable
defects.root_cause: the record was written with an inline literal string and read field-by-field with defaults
defects.fix: the document is drillmaster-signing-status/v2; v1 and unknown schemas are refused rather than reinterpreted; the shared validator requires the field set, booleans, counts, a lowercase SHA-256 manifest binding, a full source SHA, a bounded reason for every UNKNOWN, complete container provenance, and agreement between aggregate, examined_count and archive_count; the generator validates before it writes

defects.symptom: attributing the state required the artifact bytes, which the sandbox cannot retrieve
defects.root_cause: diagnostics were published only into files inside the artifact
defects.fix: a capability probe records the PowerShell version and Get-Command result; the aggregate, harness and per-file reasons reach signing-status.json, the machine-readable console line, the step summary, the single Signature status annotation, and a Signature state needs review warning for UNKNOWN or FAIL; credential values are redacted from every published string

defects.symptom: release documentation used UNSIGNED for the repository configuration and UNKNOWN for a query result as if they named one fact
defects.root_cause: one word described two layers: build configuration and observed signature state
defects.fix: four layers are named and documented separately (raw Windows answer, normalized per-file, aggregate, report-level absence); NOT_VERIFIED is confined to an absent record and cannot appear as a per-file or aggregate status; the runbook and PRODUCTION_READINESS.md state both facts side by side

defects.symptom: the report trusted the archive binding asserted by the signing record instead of checking it
defects.root_cause: no comparison existed between the record's digests and the digests the report recomputed from the release directory
defects.fix: read_signing_evidence takes the verified installer and bundle digests, the manifest digest and the source SHA as binding, and refuses a record whose installer row hashes a different file, whose container row names a different archive or digest, whose manifest binding or source SHA differs, or which omits either shipped executable

callers: packaging/windows_release_evidence.py main (before publishing a NOT_RUN record)
refusals: a superseded v1 or unknown schema, with no silent reinterpretation
an aggregate the per-file findings do not support, in either direction
UNKNOWN published without a bounded reason
duplicate file rows, unknown or missing fields at either level
malformed SHA-256 values, negative or non-integer sizes, non-boolean flags
a container archive counted in the executable aggregate, or signature_bearing contradicting the status
incomplete container provenance, or a member whose name is not the recorded file
a NOT_RUN record that also carries per-file findings or a zero-count mismatch
a diagnostic longer than the published bound
record_contract.not_run_shape: schema, method, status NOT_RUN, policy, empty files and counts, and one bounded reason; binding digests are meaningless for a run that examined no bytes and are not required

policy_preserved.signature_state_never_reddens_the_gate: a recorded state, including FAIL, is a distribution-trust finding; only an evidence failure (no record, unparseable record, contract violation) fails the step
policy_preserved.powershell_exit_codes_not_suppressed: the step snapshots $LASTEXITCODE, throws for its own evidence failures, and ends with an explicit exit 0 as before
policy_preserved.key_material_handling: no certificate, private key, PFX or password is read, printed or stored; published diagnostics are redacted against the values of the credential-named environment variables, whose names stay recorded
policy_preserved.extraction_guards: the archive-bound extraction rules from M42.3 are unchanged; no broad rewrite of already-bounded guards was made

focused_release_and_packaging_set.skipped_reason: test_real_windows_bundle_smoke_when_provided is skipped on purpose: no real Windows bundle exists in the Linux sandbox, and the skip is reported as a skip, never as a pass

windows_gate_module_scope_local.failure_attribution: all eight failures are Qt widget tests failing on libGL.so.1, absent from this sandbox and installed by the Windows and ubuntu-24.04 CI jobs; none is in the release-evidence modules changed by this mission
windows_gate_module_scope_local.environment: PYTHONUTF8=0 LC_ALL=C as the Windows job runs it, Python 3.11 sandbox venv from requirements-lock.txt plus pytest 9.1.1 and ruff 0.16.6
windows_gate_module_scope_local.command_environment: the 27 modules of the Windows gate's regression step, run locally with PYTHONUTF8=0 LC_ALL=C

internal_gates.ci: both gates were re-run on the final SHA of this mission; their identifiers are recorded in the mission report for that SHA, not here

mutation_validation.pairing_note: the two harness layers (bounded stderr on a parseable payload, and the required-field check) are redundant by design; the battery mutates them together as one entry because either one alone still attributes the cause
what_it_proves: case-insensitive normalization, the Unknown-to-UNKNOWN rule, and the unrecognised-spelling rule are each required
empty-examination and mixed-unknown aggregation are required
every refusal in the record contract - schema, duplicates, bounds, reason, signature_bearing, counts, container provenance, aggregate contradiction - is load-bearing
stderr carrying, the required-field layer, the QueryError preference, the probe, redaction, and the writer's self-validation are load-bearing
each binding the report newly verifies - manifest digest, source SHA, installer digest, bundle coverage, container archive - is load-bearing
retaining the diagnostic fields, refusing to promote an absent record, and the workflow's reason and warning channels are load-bearing
